summary: Service oriented Laravel on DigitalOcean App Platform with DigitalOcean Managed PostgreSQL as the database; front end: React + Vite, Progressive Web App.

frontend.justification: Web: A client-rendered app behind login needs no server rendering. Fit for this project: strong cost for React + Vite (priority 3); strong performance for React + Vite (priority 5); well suited to gaming projects; strong time to market for React + Vite (priority 4). Mobile: Reuses the web app, installable without an app store. Fit for this project: strong time to market for Progressive Web App (priority 4); reuses the web codebase; strong cost for Progressive Web App (priority 3); strong maintainability for Progressive Web App (priority 3).

alternatives.why_not: Scored 0.7 points lower: the team would have to learn JavaScript/TypeScript; the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to gaming projects).
Scored 0.8 points lower: the team would have to learn JavaScript/TypeScript; the chosen option wins on project.platforms (reuses the web codebase).

tradeoffs: Client-rendered: no SEO for public pages.
The team would have to learn JavaScript/TypeScript.
iOS limits background sync and push; browsers may evict offline storage.
Weaker camera/GPS/background-upload control than a native app.

backend.justification: Batteries-included PHP framework with queues and auth. Fit for this project: team.languages includes PHP; strong time to market for Laravel (priority 4); built-in authentication; strong maintainability for Laravel (priority 3).

alternatives.why_not: Scored 4.8 points lower: the team would have to learn C#; the chosen option wins on team.languages (team.languages includes PHP).
Scored 4.1 points lower: the team would have to learn JavaScript/TypeScript; proprietary API increases lock-in; the chosen option wins on team.languages (team.languages includes PHP).

tradeoffs: Long-lived WebSockets run in Laravel Reverb, a separate first-party process.
Per-request overhead is tight for p95=150ms.

database.justification: ACID transactions, JSONB, full-text search, PostGIS and pgvector in one engine. Fit for this project: strong maintainability for PostgreSQL (priority 3); strong performance for PostgreSQL (priority 5); strong security for PostgreSQL (priority 3); strong time to market for PostgreSQL (priority 4).

alternatives.why_not: Scored 0.7 points lower: the chosen option wins on priorities.maintainability (strong maintainability for PostgreSQL (priority 3)).
Scored 1.0 points lower: the chosen option wins on priorities.maintainability (strong maintainability for PostgreSQL (priority 3)).

tradeoffs: Horizontal write scaling needs partitioning, read replicas or Citus.

hosting.justification: Simple PaaS with a Bengaluru (BLR1) region and managed Postgres. Fit for this project: strong time to market for DigitalOcean App Platform (priority 4); strong performance for DigitalOcean App Platform (priority 5); strong cost for DigitalOcean App Platform (priority 3); strong scalability for DigitalOcean App Platform (priority 3).

alternatives.why_not: Scored 2.9 points lower: close runner-up; the chosen option combines better with the rest of the stack.
Scored 3.3 points lower: close runner-up; the chosen option combines better with the rest of the stack.

tradeoffs: Fewer managed services than AWS/GCP/Azure (no managed search or ML).

supporting.justification: Uses the backend framework's maintained auth library, so user data stays in your own database.
tradeoffs: Account recovery and MFA flows must still be designed.

supporting.choice: Yjs (CRDT) + Hocuspocus sync server, Redis pub/sub between nodes
supporting.justification: Concurrent edits to one board must merge without conflicts: Yjs CRDTs do that, Hocuspocus (TypeScript) syncs documents and awareness (live cursors) over WebSockets, and Redis fans updates out across instances for 4000 concurrent users. Board snapshots persist to the database.

alternatives.why_not: Managed and fast to start, but per-MAU pricing and US data storage.
Months of work to get conflict handling right.

tradeoffs: Long-lived connections need sticky sessions or a pub/sub layer.

supporting.justification: Caches hot reads and sessions to hold p95=150ms, and doubles as the pub/sub and job-queue broker.

alternatives.why_not: No pub/sub or persistence, so it cannot double as a broker.
Every read hits the database at peak.

tradeoffs: Another stateful component to size and monitor.

supporting.justification: Moves slow or retry-prone work (payment webhooks, notifications, image processing, scoring) off the request path so p95 stays low and failures retry safely.

alternatives.why_not: Event-streaming platform: heavy to run for job queues at this scale.

tradeoffs: Jobs must be idempotent; monitor the dead-letter queue.

supporting.justification: Free push delivery to Android for job updates and reminders.

alternatives.why_not: Costs per message and DLT templates.

tradeoffs: Notification payloads must not contain sensitive data.

supporting.justification: Runs tests and deploys on every merge; free minutes cover a small team.
Free Developer plan catches crashes in the app and mobile clients with stack traces.

alternatives.why_not: Strong product but expensive per host at this budget.

assumptions: Scale level L3: ~80000 users, ~4000 peak concurrent, ~800 req/s at peak, ~156.2 GB stored
List prices for the smallest production tier that fits; no reserved-instance or startup credits; excludes domains, app-store fees, SMS and payment-gateway transaction fees
